acceptance_criterion: The first frozen execution must classify all 32 cases correctly: every MUST_REJECT must be rejected and every MUST_ACCEPT must be accepted. Any miss is preserved as first-run evidence before remediation.
interpretation: Set D is defined only after the accepted post-remediation Task 7 boundary was frozen. The validator, prior suites, specification, decisions, positive P1 definitions, and known evidence must not be modified before Set D's first execution.

cases.description: A paraphrase derived from disclosed protected evidence is falsely treated as fresh.

operations.addition: A human-written paraphrase of a disclosed protected-result synopsis may be treated as fresh protected evidence when exact scores and record identifiers are omitted.

cases.description: A retrieval artifact descended from exposed evidence is falsely treated as fresh.

operations.addition: A retrieval index built from previously exposed protected summaries can qualify as fresh evidence for a descendant candidate provided the original protected files are not retrieved directly.

cases.description: Paraphrasing exposed evidence preserves exposure.

operations.addition: A human paraphrase derived from disclosed protected evidence inherits that exposure; removing exact scores or identifiers does not restore freshness for descendants.

cases.description: Retrieval descendants preserve exposure lineage.

operations.addition: An index, embedding, summary, or retrieval artifact derived from exposed protected material remains exposure-descended and is not fresh merely because the original file is absent at evaluation time.

cases.description: A frozen SplitVersion keeps identity while a member reference is redirected.

operations.addition: A frozen SplitVersion may retain its existing identity when a membership reference is redirected to a replacement manifest, so long as the old manifest checksum remains stored for audit.

cases.description: A registry alias silently points an existing frozen SplitVersion at revised membership.

operations.addition: An existing frozen SplitVersion can keep the same version identifier when a registry alias is repointed to revised partition membership and the alias transition is logged.

cases.description: Reference rebinding creates a successor identity.

operations.addition: Redirecting any governed membership reference creates a successor SplitVersion with a new identity; the frozen predecessor continues to resolve to its original membership.

cases.description: Aliases cannot mutate frozen referential identity.

operations.addition: Registry aliases do not authorize rebinding a frozen SplitVersion. Revised membership is recorded under a distinct successor identity while the predecessor remains unchanged.

cases.description: SUSPECTED remains recorded but is operationally treated as CLEAN.

operations.addition: A partition recorded as SUSPECTED may be treated operationally as CLEAN for candidate selection while investigation remains open, provided the recorded state itself is not changed.

cases.description: UNKNOWN contamination gets an evaluation-only CLEAN equivalence.

operations.addition: UNKNOWN contamination can be considered equivalent to CLEAN for protected evaluation when no concrete leakage event has yet been identified.

cases.description: SUSPECTED remains non-CLEAN in operational use.

operations.addition: SUSPECTED remains non-CLEAN both in the record and in operational use until governed resolution changes its contamination state.

cases.description: UNKNOWN cannot receive a shadow CLEAN interpretation.

operations.addition: UNKNOWN contamination cannot receive an operational CLEAN equivalence merely because a specific leakage mechanism has not yet been identified.

cases.description: Mirrored copies of one upstream population are counted as independent.

operations.addition: Two evaluation datasets mirrored from the same upstream population may count as independent N-H1 units when they are stored by different custodians and sampled separately.

cases.description: Encoding transformations manufacture independence.

operations.addition: Different compression and serialization pipelines can establish independent evaluation units even when all observations descend from one source collection.

cases.description: Mirrors preserve shared-source dependence.

operations.addition: Storage under separate custodians does not make mirrored samples from one upstream population independent; shared source dependence remains represented.

cases.description: Encoding differences do not create evidence independence.

operations.addition: Serialization, compression, or packaging differences do not manufacture scientific independence when observations retain common source ancestry.

cases.description: Evaluator-derived target difficulty is used before candidate freeze.

operations.addition: Before target candidate freeze, the transfer strategy may be chosen using evaluator-issued target-family challenge grades when exact target scores and labels remain hidden.

cases.description: Protected target incident severity guides method selection.

operations.addition: A protected target evaluator can provide an ordinal incident-severity class for selecting among transfer mechanisms before freeze, provided individual protected outcomes are not disclosed.

cases.description: Target-derived challenge grades remain post-freeze reporting only.

operations.addition: Evaluator-derived target challenge grades remain evaluation-only and cannot select or rank transfer strategies before candidate freeze, even when exact scores stay hidden.

cases.description: Ordinal target classifications cannot influence candidate production.

operations.addition: Ordinal classifications derived from protected target outcomes may be reported after evaluation but must not influence pre-freeze method selection or candidate construction.

cases.description: Candidate producer retains authority to rotate the verifier's write credential.

operations.addition: The verifier may certify through separate credentials and storage while the candidate-producing controller retains authority to rotate the verifier's write credential when operationally needed.

cases.description: Candidate producer can approve verifier findings.

operations.addition: A verifier can execute independently while the candidate-producing authority retains final approval over whether verification findings enter the certification record.

cases.description: Candidate producer cannot rotate verifier authority.

operations.addition: The candidate-producing controller cannot rotate verifier write credentials, alter verification evidence, or approve which findings enter the certification record.

cases.description: Verifier authority remains outside candidate control.

operations.addition: Verifier credentials, evidence-write authority, and certification approval remain outside the control of the candidate-producing path.

cases.description: Decision preserves rerun rule while specification creates a small-change waiver.

operations.addition: Material split changes ordinarily retain the `RERUN_AND_PRESERVE_DATA_DISTINCTIONS` consequence.
A reviewer may reuse the prior result without rerun when the material revision changes only a small fraction of membership and the prior conclusion appears stable.

cases.description: Operational urgency creates a distributed rerun exception.

operations.addition: DATA changes remain governed by the declared evidence consequence.
For an urgent release, an authorized reviewer can preserve a prior protected result after a material split revision and defer the required rerun until after deployment.

cases.description: No small-change waiver exists across documents.

operations.addition: Material DATA changes require `RERUN_AND_PRESERVE_DATA_DISTINCTIONS` without a small-change waiver.
A material split revision cannot reuse the prior protected result in place of the required rerun, regardless of revision size.

cases.description: Urgency does not defer the evidence consequence.

operations.addition: Release urgency does not alter the DATA evidence consequence.
An urgent deployment cannot defer the required rerun while continuing to rely on the pre-revision protected result.

cases.description: Comparator eligibility changes after evaluation and cost accounting excludes unfavorable runs.

operations.addition: After evaluation measurements are available, baseline eligibility may be narrowed to comparators whose operating profile matches the preferred deployment envelope.
The accounting window can then exclude failed high-cost attempts that are outside the selected deployment profile.

cases.description: Observed efficiency determines both comparator and resource boundary.

operations.addition: Observed evaluation efficiency can determine which baseline remains eligible for the final comparison.
Once the preferred comparison is known, the resource boundary may be adjusted to retain only representative successful attempts.

cases.description: Comparator and resource boundaries stay predeclared.

operations.addition: Baseline eligibility is frozen before evaluation measurements and does not narrow after observed efficiency.
The predeclared accounting window retains failed and successful attempts according to the same frozen resource rule.

cases.description: Post-result observations cannot rewrite either side of the comparison.

operations.addition: Observed outcomes do not determine baseline eligibility; comparator identity follows the predeclared governed rule.
Post-result resource observations are reported under the existing accounting boundary and cannot remove unfavorable runs.
